_comment: Applicability baseline for the pinned MCP conformance runner against bin/main.exe.
Read by compare_application.py; every check names its class, the status this run
observed, and why it is or is not an obligation of seekwright's three-tool surface.
An applicable check must pass; an excluded check must keep its recorded status.
oracle-parity means the Python implementation fails identically; port-divergence
means it behaves differently and the difference is recorded, not silently excluded.
Recorded 2026-11-13 from the run described in README.md, 'The application baseline'.

classes.applicable: An obligation of the three-tool surface or the transport; must pass.
classes.mixed: A scenario whose checks are split between applicable obligations and exclusions.
classes.fixture-declaration: Needs a tool, resource, prompt or annotation only the official fixture declares.
classes.absent-feature: Needs a capability outside the frozen surface (resources, prompts, rich content, progress, MRTR, completion, tasks).
classes.oracle-parity: A failing check the Python implementation fails identically, so it cannot distinguish the port.
classes.port-divergence: A failing check where the Python implementation behaves differently; excluded from the three-tool contract but recorded as a known difference.

dns-rebinding-protection.reason: Rejecting a non-local Host/Origin is an applicable transport obligation; accepting a loopback Host with a port-bearing Origin fails identically in the Python implementation, so that check is oracle parity.

localhost-host-rebinding-rejected.reason: A non-local Host/Origin is refused with 403 before the request reaches the MCP handler; this is the transport's DNS-rebinding obligation.

localhost-host-valid-accepted.reason: The runner sends Origin http://127.0.0.1:8811; both implementations seed their Origin allowlist with bare loopback origins (http://127.0.0.1) and refuse the port-bearing Origin with 403. Measured against the Python oracle with the same runner: identical failure, so it does not distinguish the port.
